newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on tight market liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on tight market liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 50 basis points at 19.75 percent in early trade on Wednesday due to speculative pressure stemming from liquidity pressures, traders said.
"As today is the cutoff date for central bank balances, some brokers are short on cash which lends itself to speculation by others," a trader said.
Banks have to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with Banco de Mexico on Wednesday.
Other traders said upside pressure on secondary rates could ease later in the session due to a favorable reaction on the U.S. bond market to mild U.S. producer price data.

Dealers said the recent crop of U.S. economic data had relieved concerns the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee would raise U.S. interest rates by more than 25 basis points to contain inflationary pressure in the U.S. economy.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 18/32 to yield 6.88 percent.

"U.S. (Producer Price Index) data should have made overnight Cetes rates fall immediately, but with the central bank's cut-off date today, the market is focusing on that rather than external factors," a fixed-income analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile declined 10 basis points to 20.50 percent.
Liquidity of 1.866 billion pesos was due to return to the system from central bank operations in prior sessions.
